doc.title: Rebecca Kilgore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997

title: Not thinking of herself as a jazz singer
summary: She does not consider herself a jazz singer; she sticks close to the melody and tries to be a good singer.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Yeah that’s interesting because I really don’t in some ways consider myself a jazz singer. Of course that’s a very controversial tag. You know, who knows what that means? I don’t improvises all that much and I stick pretty close to the melody, but I’m not like a show singer. I don’t belt it out. So I’m somewhere in another world.
Best to be a good singer I guess. I mean Nancy Wilson doesn’t think of herself as a jazz singer either.
In fact she doesn’t like it when you call her that. She says “I’m a singer.” And whatever she chooses to do, she tries to do it well.
Well I try to be a good singer.
